title: What Happens at an MOT Test: A Walkthrough
excerpt: An MOT is a set inspection of your car's safety and emissions, taking about 45 to 60 minutes. Here's exactly what the tester checks and what the results mean.
contentHtml:
At an MOT, a tester inspects your car against government safety and emissions standards - it takes about 45 to 60 minutes and ends in a pass or fail, plus any advisories. No parts are changed; it's an inspection only. You wait or drop the car off, and the result is logged to the DVSA database (visible afterwards on RegScan).

How long does it take?

A standard car (Class 4) MOT takes roughly 45 to 60 minutes. If the centre is busy you may be asked to leave the car for a few hours. Repairs and a retest, if needed, take longer.

What the tester checks

The tester works through set items against DVSA standards, without dismantling the car:

  • Lights - headlights, indicators, brake lights, reflectors and aim
  • Brakes - condition, performance and balance (often on a roller machine)
  • Tyres and wheels - tread depth, condition and correct size
  • Steering and suspension - wear and operation
  • Seatbelts - condition and that they latch
  • Windscreen, wipers and washers - view and cleaning
  • Exhaust and emissions - noise and pollutant levels
  • Body and structure - corrosion in key areas, sharp edges
  • Number plates, horn, mirrors and VIN

What they don't check

An MOT does not assess engine, clutch or gearbox condition, or general mechanical reliability - that's what a service is for. It's purely a safety and emissions inspection at a point in time.

Understanding the result

  • Pass - you get a certificate; any advisories are noted for you to monitor.
  • Fail - caused by a Major or Dangerous defect; must be repaired and retested. A dangerous defect means you must not drive it away.

After the test

The result is recorded against your registration in the DVSA MOT history within minutes. You can view it - along with past results, mileage and recurring advisories - free on RegScan. Check your vehicle.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does an MOT take?

About 45 to 60 minutes for a standard car, longer if the centre is busy or repairs and a retest are needed.

What does an MOT check?

Safety and emissions items: lights, brakes, tyres, steering, suspension, seatbelts, windscreen, exhaust, body structure and more - against DVSA standards.

What isn't checked in an MOT?

Engine, clutch and gearbox condition and general reliability aren't assessed. That's the job of a service, not the MOT.

Can I wait while my car is tested?

Often yes - many centres let you wait the 45 to 60 minutes, though busy centres may ask you to leave the car.

When can I see my MOT result?

Within minutes it's logged to the DVSA database. Check it free on RegScan by entering your registration.
